common.ops_best_practices: Best practices: anticipate peaks (seasonality, public holidays), use proper export packaging (blocking, strapping), secure ad valorem insurance and keep a buffer on critical deadlines.
common.incoterms_intro: Incoterms shift control, cost allocation and risk transfer along the chain. Typical patterns: FOB/CIF for standard sea flows; DAP/DDP for door-to-door experience.
incoterms_list: FOB: buyer controls main carriage; requires logistics maturity
CFR: seller pays main carriage; risk transfers at loading
CIF: seller pays freight + insurance; risk transfers at loading
DAP/DDP: extended coverage by seller; import clearance and taxes depending on variant
common.delivered_cost_note: Always compare FCL vs LCL on total delivered cost, not only on the rate per m³.

common.cbm_note: Indicative only: 20' ≈ 33 m³, 40' ≈ 67 m³. Tolerances and weight/volume limits depend on carrier and service.

france_china.label: France ↔ China
france_china.title: Sea freight France ↔ China (FCL & LCL)
france_china.subtitle: Reliable FCL/LCL solutions between key French ports (Le Havre, Marseille-Fos, Dunkerque) and Chinese hubs (Shanghai, Ningbo, Shenzhen, Qingdao).
france_china.transit: Indicative transit times: 35–50 days depending on routing, season and congestion.
costs: On the France ↔ China corridor, FCL often becomes optimal above roughly 13–15 m³: fewer handlings, higher security and more stable lead times. Below that, LCL (groupage) is an effective lever to control costs.
Rates vary with season, carrier and vessel load (BAF/CAF/PSS). Use the CBM calculator and request a quote for a transparent, up-to-date estimate.
customs: We handle BL, invoice, packing list, certificates of origin (if required) and compliance checks. Common Incoterms: FOB/CIF; DAP/DDP for extended door-to-door coverage. Customs clearance support included.
insurance_risks: Ad valorem cargo insurance: coverage from departure to delivery
Export packaging advice to reduce damage and disputes
why_us: Planning around peaks (CNY, Q4) and alternative services when needed
Rail options in complement to gain time on sensitive flows
Carrier and hub network to smooth congestion impacts
use_cases: Regular programs: FCL to secure capacity/lead times; occasional rail as a faster alternative
Product launches: LCL for pilots, then switch to FCL as volume ramps up
Sensitive cargo: FCL + professional packing + ad valorem insurance

planning: Anticipate demand peaks (CNY, Q4) and secure slots in advance
Compare direct vs transhipment services depending on Chinese port
Keep calendar buffer to absorb congestion and weather events

BL: validate draft before issue to avoid costly amendments
Insurance: size coverage according to cargo value and sensitivity

faq.q: FCL or LCL: what to choose on the France–China corridor?
faq.a: Above roughly 13–15 m³, FCL is often more economical and more secure (fewer handlings). Below that, LCL remains relevant to optimise budget.

faq.q: Which Incoterms should I use (FOB/CIF/DAP/DDP)?
faq.a: FOB/CIF are common on China flows; DAP/DDP offer extended coverage. The choice depends on desired control and risk profile.

faq.q: Do you manage customs documentation?
faq.a: Yes: BL, commercial invoice, packing list, any required certificates; plus compliance checks and customs assistance.

faq.q: Can rail freight replace sea freight?
faq.a: On some corridors, rail offers around 18–22 days transit. It is a good compromise between air and sea in terms of speed and cost.

faq.q: Which periods are the most constrained?
faq.a: Chinese New Year and Q4 before Christmas. It's better to book early and keep alternative services available.

faq.q: Do you provide cargo insurance?
faq.a: Yes, ad valorem coverage from departure to delivery, with packing advice to reduce risk.

france_congo.label: France ↔ Congo
france_congo.title: Sea transport & freight France ↔ Congo (Pointe-Noire) – Groupage, moves, vehicles
france_congo.subtitle: LCL groupage, FCL full containers, international moves and vehicle/motorbike shipping to Pointe-Noire from France and Europe (France/Benelux), for both businesses and individuals, including parcels, baggage and personal effects in containers or groupage. As a France‑based freight forwarder, we prioritise reliable and transparent schemes on the France–Congo corridor rather than purely chasing the lowest nominal rate.
france_congo.transit: Indicative transit times: 20–30 days depending on departures, stops and season.
costs: To Pointe-Noire, LCL (groupage) is particularly relevant for small volumes, personal effects, baggage and B2B parcels. Above roughly 13–15 m³, FCL usually becomes more competitive and offers more predictable lead times.

Costs should be assessed as total delivered cost: sea freight, surcharges, port THC, pre/post-carriage and duties/taxes on import into Congo. We help you arbitrate between LCL/FCL and departure ports (France/Benelux) according to your budget and milestones.

Whether you are shipping personal effects, e‑commerce parcels, industrial pallets or a full move with vehicles, we build a transparent cost breakdown and clearly explain what is included (freight, surcharges, handling, pre/post‑carriage, estimated duties and taxes).
customs: Strict and detailed documentation control: commercial invoice, packing list, BL, certificate of origin where required, and cargo-specific documents. Customs representation and support on duties & taxes with local counterparts in Pointe-Noire.
insurance_risks: Ad valorem cargo insurance sized to the value of your goods
Export packaging advice to reduce damage and disputes

services_block.title: End-to-end logistics services for your shipments to Congo (Pointe-Noire)
services_block.intro: For your flows to Pointe-Noire, we do more than just book a container: we coordinate the whole logistics chain from France and Europe to the Congolese port, including:
items: Pick-up and delivery of partial loads (pallets, cartons, small B2B lots, personal effects) across France and the Benelux.
Pre- and post-carriage for FCL containers to the departure port and from Pointe-Noire port, organising road transport where feasible via our partner network.
Transport documentation management (ocean bill of lading, packing list, commercial invoice, certificate of origin and cargo-specific documents).
Export customs clearance in France and support with import formalities in Congo through our local partners.
LCL sea freight services to Pointe-Noire for intermediate volumes, with consolidation and warehousing options in France or the Benelux before departure.
Handling of export, import and, on a case-by-case basis, cross-trade operations involving Congo.
Assistance with local specific requirements (documents, certificates, port constraints) in coordination with actors present in Pointe-Noire.

why_us: Dedicated positioning on the France–Congo corridor for parcels, B2B cargo, international moves, vehicles and motorbikes.
Strong expertise in LCL/parcel flows to Pointe-Noire with regular consolidations.
B2B pickup in France's main economic hubs and, on request, in the Benelux.
Documentary coaching and local customs assistance via partners based in Pointe-Noire.
use_cases: International moves and personal effects (boxes, furniture, household goods) in LCL or FCL to Pointe-Noire, with pickup options in France and the Benelux.
Parcels/small lots: LCL groupage to Pointe-Noire with visibility on milestones and proactive follow-up.
B2B shipments (pallets, spare parts, consumables, equipment) in LCL or FCL depending on volume and flow regularity.
Heavy equipment and machinery: FCL/Open Top or special equipment after feasibility study, with orchestrated pickup.
Vehicles and motorbikes: tailor-made Ro-Ro or container solutions where feasible, with documentation management and coordination upon arrival.

planning: Plan consolidations to limit waiting time between departures
Ensure clear parcel traceability and labelling
Validate local documentary requirements in advance
documentation: Reinforced export packaging, dated photos, seals if needed
Switch to FCL when value/volume justifies it to reduce handlings
Coordinate B2B pickup in time slots compatible with terminal reception

faq.q: Is LCL suitable for Congo?
faq.a: Yes, groupage is relevant for parcels and small volumes. We operate regular consolidations with visibility on key milestones.

faq.q: Do you handle pickup and packaging?
faq.a: We offer B2B pickup in French hubs and export packaging to limit damage and meet port requirements.

faq.q: What visibility do we have on tracking and notifications?
faq.a: Real-time tracking, updates at key steps (loading, transit, arrival) and proactive follow-up.

faq.q: Which documents are required for import into Congo?
faq.a: BL, invoice, packing list, certificate of origin if required, and goods-specific documents. Customs assistance is available.

faq.q: Do you recommend insurance?
faq.a: Yes, an ad valorem policy is recommended. We size coverage according to value and sensitivity of goods.

faq.q: When should we switch from LCL to FCL towards Pointe-Noire?
faq.a: Around 13–15 m³, FCL often becomes competitive and more predictable; below that, LCL remains attractive.

faq.q: How much does it cost to ship a 20' or 40' container to Pointe-Noire?
faq.a: The cost of a 20' or 40' container to Pointe-Noire depends on the departure port (Le Havre, Fos, Benelux), season, cargo type and the services included (pre/post-carriage, customs, cargo insurance). We always provide itemised quotes (ocean freight, surcharges, THC, estimated duties & taxes) so you have a clear view of total delivered cost.

faq.q: Which lead time should we plan for a full move from France to Congo?
faq.a: On average, you should allow 20–30 days of sea transit to Pointe-Noire, plus time for pickup, stuffing, port operations and customs clearance on arrival. We recommend planning a buffer for potential inspections and to contact us as soon as your approximate departure dates are known.

faq.q: Do you offer a combined move + vehicle + insurance package for Congo?
faq.a: Yes, we can design a scheme combining an FCL container (personal effects + 1 or 2 vehicles), customs clearance and ad valorem cargo insurance. The goal is to give you a clear package (container, port services, formalities, coverage) rather than a bare "port-to-port" rate that is hard to compare.

faq.q: What are the main strengths of the France–Turkey corridor?
faq.a: Short lead times, high frequencies, strong multimodal alternatives. Ideal for regular flows and agile supply chains.

faq.q: Do you offer multimodal schemes?
faq.a: Yes: Sea/Road to optimise cost, and air for urgent shipments. We orchestrate the mix according to your constraints.

faq.q: Is cross-trade possible (e.g. China→Turkey→Europe/Africa)?
faq.a: Yes, on a case-by-case basis with robust documentation and the right carriers/partners.

faq.q: Which documents and Incoterms do you recommend?
faq.a: BL, invoice, packing list; Incoterms (FOB/CIF/DAP/DDP) can be chosen according to your preferred risk and responsibility split.

faq.q: FCL vs LCL on Turkey: what should we favour?
faq.a: FCL for significant volumes and more stable lead times; LCL is competitive for small or irregular shipments.

faq.q: How do you manage insurance and risk?
faq.a: We recommend ad valorem coverage, plus packaging and documentation guidance to avoid disputes and delays.

faq.q: Is LCL suitable for Angola?
faq.a: Yes. Groupage is relevant for personal effects, small lots and professional parcels. We operate regular departures to Luanda with visibility on key milestones.

faq.q: When should we switch from LCL to FCL to Luanda?
faq.a: In practice, FCL often becomes attractive above roughly 13–15 m³, considering total delivered cost and the sensitivity of the goods.

faq.q: Which documents are required for Angola?
faq.a: Detailed commercial invoice, packing list, BL, certificates of origin or specific documents depending on the goods, and paperwork required by Angolan authorities. We guide you through this checklist.

faq.q: Can you handle vehicles or personal effects?
faq.a: Yes, subject to feasibility review: vehicles in containers or Ro-Ro, motorbikes on their wheels without dismantling whenever possible, personal effects in LCL or FCL. We clarify customs and regulatory constraints upfront.

faq.q: Do you recommend insurance for Angola?
faq.a: Yes, an ad valorem policy is strongly recommended on this corridor. We help size coverage and document packaging to reduce disputes.

faq.q: How much does it cost to ship a 20' or 40' container to Luanda?
faq.a: The cost of a 20' or 40' container to Luanda depends on the departure port (Le Havre, Fos, Antwerp, Rotterdam), season, cargo type and the services included (pre/post-carriage, customs, cargo insurance). We provide detailed, itemised quotes (ocean freight, surcharges, THC, estimated duties & taxes) so you have a clear view of total delivered cost.

faq.q: Which lead time should we plan for a full move from France to Angola?
faq.a: On average, you should allow 20–25 days of sea transit to Luanda, plus time for pickup, stuffing, port operations and customs clearance on arrival. We recommend planning a buffer for potential inspections and scheduling your move as soon as your approximate dates are known.
